views.markdown:
Lisa lets you theme macOS with CSS. Buttons, checkboxes, title bars, sidebars, menus, even SF Symbols: every app picks it up, and changes show up live while you edit.

It comes with 11 themes to start: Catalina, Celadon, Blueprint, Lacquer, Riso, Aurora, Cassette, Paperwork, Nocturne, Moss and Synth. Every one has a light and a dark version.

If you want to make your own, open Lisa Editor. It shows a real window that updates as you type, and you can tweak every control, the window buttons and the window shape from there.

You can switch themes from Terminal too:

```
lisa themes
lisa use Celadon
```

After installing, log out and back in, then pick a theme.

### Good to know

Lisa runs a small background service (`monalisad`) that draws the themes for every app. It also turns off SwiftUI's Liquid Glass look so apps go back to the classic layout. Uninstalling turns it back on.

Your own themes go in `/Users/Shared/Lisa/Themes`, and they stay put if you uninstall.

Needs Ammonia, and an Apple silicon Mac on macOS 26 or newer.
